Determination of Silicon by the Silicomolybdenum Blue Spectrophotometric Method
Silicon is an important element in iron ores and steel materials, and its content significantly affects steel properties. In the commonly used silicomolybdenum blue spectrophotometric method, silicic acid reacts with ammonium molybdate in acidic medium to form silicomolybdenum yellow, which is then reduced to silicomolybdenum blue for absorbance measurement. This problem concerns sample fusion, removal of interferences, control of color-development conditions, and quantification by a calibration curve.

subquestions.text_open:
4.1 Sample pretreatment
Weigh 0.1284 g of sample into a 50 mL silver crucible, add 2 g of sodium peroxide and mix, then cover with another 0.5 g of sodium peroxide. Cover the crucible, place it in a furnace at 300 °C, slowly raise the temperature to 750 °C-800 °C, and fuse for 20 min. Remove and allow to cool slightly. Add 100 mL of boiling water to leach the melt completely and wash out the crucible. While swirling, slowly add 30 mL of concentrated hydrochloric acid. After cooling, transfer the solution to a 200 mL volumetric flask, dilute to the mark with water, mix, filter, and discard the initial portion of the filtrate.
4.1.6 The acidified solution must be dry-filtered through medium-speed filter paper, and the first few milliliters of filtrate must be discarded. Explain the purposes of this procedure. If the initial filtrate were not discarded, would the measured result be too high or too low?

4.2 Color development for the sample
Transfer 10.00 mL of filtrate to a 100 mL volumetric flask and add blank-test solution to bring the volume to 20 mL. Add 10 mL of hydrochloric acid (1 + 3), add potassium permanganate solution (20 g/L) dropwise until the solution is pale red, add 10 mL of water, and mix.
Add 1 mL of anhydrous ethanol and mix. While continuously swirling, add 5 mL of ammonium molybdate solution (100 g/L), mix, and allow to stand at 15 °C-25 °C for 15 min.
Add 15 mL of hydrochloric acid (1 + 3), followed by 5 mL of oxalic acid-tartaric acid mixture containing 50 g/L oxalic acid and 40 g/L tartaric acid. Mix and immediately add 5 mL of ascorbic acid solution (20 g/L), dilute to the mark with water, mix, and allow to stand at 25 °C-35 °C for 15 min.
Transfer a portion of the colored solution to a 3 cm cuvette. Using the colored blank-test solution carried through with the sample as reference, measure an absorbance of 0.425 at 810 nm.
4.2.1 Explain why adding potassium permanganate to a pale-red endpoint eliminates interference from lower-valent iron and organic matter, and state the effect of excess potassium permanganate.

4.2.4 State which interfering ions are masked by oxalic acid and tartaric acid, respectively, in the color-development system, and explain why ascorbic acid must not be added before the oxalic acid-tartaric acid mixture.

4.3 Construction of the calibration curve
Transfer 0 mL, 1.00 mL, 2.00 mL, 4.00 mL, 6.00 mL, 8.00 mL, and 10.00 mL portions of silicon dioxide standard solution (20.0 μg/mL) to a series of 100 mL volumetric flasks. Add water to 20 mL and develop the color according to the procedure in 4.2. Transfer each colored solution to a 3 cm cuvette and measure the absorbance at 810 nm against a reagent blank. Construct a calibration curve using the amount of silicon dioxide in μg as the horizontal coordinate and absorbance as the vertical coordinate.

| Volume of silicon dioxide standard solution ($V$ / mL) | 0.00 | 1.00 | 2.00 | 4.00 | 6.00 | 8.00 | 10.00 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Amount of silicon dioxide ($m$ / μg) | 0 | 20.00 | 40.00 | 80.00 | 120.0 | 160.0 | 200.0 |
| Absorbance ($A$) | 0.000 | 0.082 | 0.163 | 0.326 | 0.488 | 0.651 | 0.812 |

Calculate the silicon dioxide content of the sample.
